actual.value:
1) 162 journalists trained
2) Fojo-IMS facilitated activities to test the feasibility of establishing a network between community radios, regional media, and universities.
1) 82 journalists (52 female) and editors were trained 2) The Media Information and Research Hub (MIRH) was launched in May 2022.

83 Journalists, including editors, were trained in topics such as fact checking and community radio management. The programme supported regional exchange which included master classes in investigative journalism and interactions in regional and international conferences (AIJC, SJP etc). An information hub (MIRH) was launched in May 2022. 200 content/publications were produced and collected in 2022 in different content trees. 2.3K engagement to the users have been registered in December 2022 over the year. We have not managed to fulfil the outputs according to indicators and the results framework during 2022 due to the situation in the country and vacant positions in the team.

Fact-checking training organised by Fojo- IMS and Africa Check took place 28-29 Jan 2021. The training was a 2-day online and IRL training. 35 editors and senior journalists were trained on the basics of fact-checking and verification. The majority of the group, 20 trainees were female. Major journalism associations, i.e., the Editors Guild, Ethiopian Media Women Association, and Community Radio Broadcasters Association attended. Conflict reporting training AMEN and the Editors Guild (EG) have submitted a proposal to hold two training workshops in April 2021 for 40 editors on peacebuilding and conflict reporting is approved. The agreement is developed with the EG to ensure equal participation of women journalists.

title.narrative: 1.2 Relations and interaction between key actors are strengthened, building understanding, trust, and respect for each other’s roles in a reformed media landscape.

Trust‐building examples between key actors to promote a reformed media landscape.
# of relevant experiences documented, analysed and used # of meetings between key actors and issues discussed during the meetings

actual.value: 14 Dec 2020 Stakeholder meeting Full day physical event, Jupitor International, Addis Ababa. Fojo-IMS organized a stakeholder’s consultation meeting ‘Building Partnerships and Alliance to a Stronger and More Professional Media Sector.’ The meeting was attended by the major partners from diversified media houses- state-owned, community, and privately-owned, journalism schools, civil society organizations, and media and journalism associations. The independent media regulator, Ethiopian Broadcasting Authority also sent a representative. 48 active participants, out of which only 8 of them were female. Full meeting report can be requested. Regional media were represented except for Benishangul, Gambella and Tigray.

During 2022 many trust building activities took place and key actors (from all parts of the media landscape and civil society) were able to meet and discuss in safe environments (both informal and formal settings). 2 major conferences, in different locations, on media reform were implemented (Bahir Dar and Addis) as well as conferences on journalism during conflict, media and political transition and media’s role in national dialogue. The programme was partner led and engaged with 687 individuals (from different regions and parts of the media). In total 21 academic papers were presented. Challenges: To find sustainability among local coalitions, many initiatives is taken without a long-term strategy or funding.

Many media-related initiatives continue to operate without a long-term strategy, and information sharing and coordination between practitioners and stakeholders remain scattered. To remedy this and ensure sustainability, the Fojo-IMS programme continued to support coalition-building, networking, advocacy, and efforts aimed at consensus-building and joint initiatives on pertinent issues, using a wide sector approach. Throughout the programme period different activities to enhance trust and build resilience and solidarity have taken place. Relations have been strengthened and numerous platforms, coalitions and discussions have been happened with key actors (see below). Since 2020 the programme has engaged in formal and informal discussions, conferences, presentations and round tables. This focus became even more important due to the changing and more restrictive political context. Another sign on increased trust, from programmatic perspective, is that Fojo and IMS project team members are regularly invited to present and be part of other organisations, non-state/state actors etc meetings, research, consultative engagements on specific topics. Actors like Ethiopia Media Council is becoming stronger and are issuing press statements about the media reform. Another example is how CARD, representing the civil society associations, also are issuing critical statements “calling for peace”, advocating for press freedom and safety”. This was unheard about pre-2018. Some of the key platforms include: • AIJC2021, co-hosted in Addis, Nov 2021 • Journalism teaching in a time of conflict, 2022, EJEN • Fojo-IMS Media Reform conference (2022 and 2023) Addis • Media Reform Conference in May 2021 in Bahir Dar • National conferences on gender/media policy, Addis, 2022 and 2024 • Reactivation of EMSA - national conference, Addis October 2023, • Radio Days Ethiopia with ECRBC, Addis in November 2023 • National media ethics conference with EMC in Addis, Dec 2023 • National conference on gender policy, Addis, December 2023 • Media Literacy and Youth festival with Mersa, Addis, Dec 2023 All these activities have been important and contributed to a crucial dialogue on the topics. The sector is today more connected and that key actor are stringer and are promoting a reformed media landscape and supported a civil society in Ethiopia, something that did not exist in 2018. Key activities in 2023 include: Editors Guild Breakfast meetings Through partnership agreement, the programme supported Editor’s Guild to organise 13 weekly Editors’ Breakfast meetings between August and December 2023. Themes included, media reform, media independence, access to information, media and gender and climate change, media and human right and many more. The platform improved communication, collaboration, and trust between editors and contributed to tackling the state of polarisation in the Ethiopian media. The programme also supported 3 members to participate in the Kenyan Editors Guild AGM in October 2023 in Mombasa Kenya. This was an important regional peer to peer meeting. Ethiopia Media Sector Alliance (EMSA) re-vitalisation IMS co-hosted with UNESCO the EMSA National Conference (19-20 Oct) at the UNECA Conference Centre. Approx. 149 participants representing diverse set of media stakeholders. Annual Media Reform Conference, 5-6 Dec Building on the theme and focus from the conference in 2022, Approx. 80 media stakeholders participated from different regions in Ethiopia. National Media Ethics Conference, 7 Dec EMC together with other partners organised the event. Approx. 50 media stakeholders discussed means on improving the state of ethical reporting and the future of journalism in Ethiopia.

title.narrative: 2.2: Targeted media advanced their models and practices for financial sustainability and audience trust

Examples of models and practices for financial sustainability implemented by targeted media, tailored to each partners' specific needs.
# of media outlets staff trained and by other means capacitated / # of audience centric product development initiatives in targeted media outlets / # and type of internal cross‐functional, cross‐media and diversification initiatives in targeted media / # of audience data, media research and audience interactions used in targeted media outlets

actual.value: Consecutive meetings (from November 2020 to March 2021) with media development partners specifically with the Media Development Investment Fund (MDIF has been coordinating media business model interventions in Ethiopia under the PRIMED program) were held to strategize support to targeted media, to avoid duplication, and to respond to the rapidly changing needs of the media busines sector in Ethiopia.

One comprehensive media viability programme implemented 2021-2024. In 2023 activities such as advanced mentoring, direct support, equipment and training took place. The programme components included: • 4 Selected media houses in Addis Ababa (Reporter, Insider, Addis Zeybe, Mensh, Addis Zeybe*) • Selected community radios (Koore, Hawassa, Wolaiya and Debremarkos and Hawassa) • Regional consultant team consisting of prominent media viability and CR experts from South Africa, Kenya and Ethiopia. • Implemented “own projects” to enhance production/strategy/viability with support from team of consultants. • Completed Wits certificate credit course for community radio managers, • Radio Days conference (Nov 23) gathering 35 community radio stations • Equipment support for partners of a value of 35 038 USD procured and distributed. Community radio support through the MV programme Community radio has become an essential part of local communities in Ethiopia, providing daily information to residents. These stations have addressed a significant gap in local news coverage, especially in small towns across the country. While independent media is still relatively young in Ethiopia, community radios are even newer and face numerous operational challenges. In recent years, there has been a growing focus on community radio, with various capacity-building activities aimed at supporting these stations. Fojo, for example, has been involved in sustainability support programs for a group of community radios, focusing on training and material assistance. One area where these efforts have made a noticeable impact is in radio programming. Stations like Kore and Wolaita have introduced new programs that focus on local issues such as dowry traditions and gender equality, which have been well-received by local audiences. Additionally, engagement with listeners has been enhanced through call-in shows, facilitated by equipment support from Fojo. This engagement has helped elevate the standing of these stations among local audiences. Koore community radio –improved their quality programming and content development taking ‘Tilosh’ as a radio magazine project. The support enabled a 10 year planning framework for sustainability of the radio station. Equipment was purchased and distributed and included: Solar energy equipment, HP laptop, Samsung tablet and WiFi dongle with one-year unlimited data subscription. The solar system has made it possible for Koore to air despite electricity cuts which was a big issue before. According to the CR manager there are now no power interruptions which means more broadcasting time. Wolaita (wogetta) community radio received a capacity building support for programme development and developing public interest production on ‘Woga’ radio magazine incorporating drama, vox pops, panel discussion, interview, and expert opinion. The support included short term and long-term sustainability planning which has according to the CR manager lead to more participatory programmes and better/direct contact with the audience. Equipment was purchased and distributed and included: Desktop, five sound recorders, and a WiFi dongle and two telephone hybrids to Wolaita Community Radio. The hybrids increased the production and broadcasting and contributed to more live broadcasting. Debremarkos implemented a radio magazine formatting of ‘Meqenet’ radio show. Capacity building of community journalism and news localization as well as digital media use to maximise audience reach and countering dis and mis information. Due to the political context, it has been very difficult time for Debremarkos CR which is in the Amhara region. The last 3 months they have been off the air due to strong government pressure. Equipment was purchased and distributed and included:11 Samsung tablets, four headphones, two condenser studio mics and three sound recorder and Wi- Fi dongle handed to Debre Markos University – the equipment support has led to that the station reached a wider audience through digital media as well as improved the quality of production according to the CR manger. See impact films produced by Mensh production here: • https://fojo.se/dokument/ethiopia/Fojo-2-Suppoted-Woga-Program- Wogata.mp4 • https://fojo.se/dokument/ethiopia/Fojo-1-Supported-Tilosh-Program- Kore.mp4 • https://fojo.se/dokument/ethiopia/Fojo-3-Material-Support-Kore- Wogeta.mp4 Hawassa Strategic planning training for Hawassa industry park radio March to July 2023 and online. Support was discontinued due to lack of engagement by board. Wits Journalism Certificate Community Manager Course 15 community radio managers (incl. 4 females) from 13 community radios from most of the regions in Ethiopia were trained, second round completed in March 2023 with follow up online assignments. All 13 successfully submitted course work and was given a certificate at the Radio Day conference in Nov 2023. Radio Days Ethiopia Conference 35 community radios and other media actors gathered in Addis in November to discuss the impact of community radios and the need to quality journalism for community radios. During the conference 5 masterclasses on different journalism development thematic area including AI and journalism, factchecking, digital storytelling, community radio management for the radio days participants to share experiences and learnings in media independence and income generation in the community radios. Media house support through the ML programme Selected media houses (The Reporter, Ethiopian Insider, Mensh) received long-term viability support in trainings on digital content development in 2023. The Reporter – digital transformation project (legacy newspaper) The Reporter, one of the largest print media organizations in Ethiopia, has undergone a transformation. Its digitization projects have diversified its digital content offerings, attracting both new and existing audiences. The revamped The Reporter YouTube channel now features regular news coverage and popular long interview features, which has helped the Fojosupported platform quickly gain 40k subscribers. Additionally, The Reporter's revenue structure, once solely reliant on print advertisements, is now shifting towards digital revenue sources, including social media monetization and web advertisements. The well-established Amharic and English websites of The Reporter are driving impressive advertisement revenue, making it a more viable player in the market. Other print media organizations are also striving to adapt their business models to the new digital environment by putting up paywalls and focusing on website advertisements. Equipment support purchased to better digitise the giant print media in Ethiopia included a digital camera, stabilizers, microphones, laptop etc. Ethiopia Insider (independent digital outlet) Platforms like Ethiopian Insider have been widely embraced in the news industry for their quality reporting and high journalistic (and independent) standards. Ethiopian Insider's resilience is particularly noteworthy, having weathered severe security incidents that nearly led to its closure. Through close support from the programme team and consultant from Nairobi Ethiopian insider implemented a project on enhancing the organisational capacity in terms editorial policy, communications' business plan, employment contracts, and organizational structure – also bringing in gender perspective. By also supporting video explainers and a revamp of the video production as well as working with diversification of digital products they have made significant achievements. In July 2023 they crossed a milestone of having more than 200 000 followers in just two weeks. The Facebook follower has steadily risen to over 230 000 reaching an impressive lifetime organic reach over 6.1 million, with an increase in their female audience – rose with 11%

The media viability programme was rolled out in 2022, to be continued all of 2023. 3 media houses and 4 community radios were selected. Support in 2022 included assessments, mentoring, education (capacity development) and preparations for direct support. Examples of models and practices for financial sustainability were developed and started to be implemented. At the end of 2022 we started to see impact but more support and time is needed in 2023. MOU signed in 2022. • The Reporter worked on a re-organisation from print to digitalisation. • Addis Zeybe worked on experimentations in digital product development, production of engaging targeted content and diversification of revenue streams and audience segments and • Ethiopia Insider worked on a corporate strategy plan, development of digital explainer formats in text, graphics, video, and audio. • Advanced community management radio training implemented with strong focus on financial sustainability

title.narrative: 1.1 Key actors/institutions established, recognized, and strengthened in fulfilling their roles, responsibilities, and mandates related to media reform

Key actors, including selected partners, actively and persistently participating in media reform process / # of individuals (aggregated by gender) at partner organisations engaged in the media reform process

actual.value: Media reform – new media law The programme has supported the media legislation process and contributed to the realization of the new liberal media proclamation through legal expert support to the Media Law Reform Working Group, which has formulated most of the legal texts as input to the reform, to provide inputs and insights from comparative experiences to media institutions, regulators and media professionals. Preparations are in progress to support EMA, Attorney General Office and other partners with institution building to increase their competencies and engagement in the implementation and next steps of the media reform. Institutional capacity support Preparations to follow up activities from 2020 and new activities planned for 2021 have started in October 2020. To improve the overall capacity of key media institutions, MoUs and capacity support is ongoing with the following key partners: • Ethiopian Media Authority (EMA) • Ethiopia Media Council (EMC) • Editors Guild of Ethiopia (EGE), • Ethiopian Community Radio Broadcasters Association (ECRBA) • Amhara National Regional Media Association (ANRMA). Study on self-regulation To address the gaps on media self-regulation, the program commissioned MMI to conduct a study on ‘Operationalizing of Self-regulation of Ethiopian Media.’ With Mersa Media Institute - it will be printed and launched in April. Self-regulation event 2 Feb 2021 (physical) Full day event at Sapphire Addis, Addis Ababa – organised by Fojo-IMS and Mersa Media Institute (MMI). Key actors from Ethiopian media and institutions gathered for the first major event. Discussion on how to establish mechanisms and collaborations for self-regulating media. The event was a landmark with promising constructive discussions between the media professionals and the official Ethiopian Media Authority (EMA). 50 particants (High level. Regulators, Editors, media managers and owners, journalists, government, CSOs, Media institutions. Academicians). Best practice from Kenya experience was also shared.

The programme has strengthened key actors’ ability to develop and implement a legislative and institutional framework that supports a free and self-regulated media and promotes informed and engaged citizenry. The programme contributed to improving the capacity of the targeted partners, media institutions, and government actors and they have actively participated in the media reform. Through trainings, research and discussions key partners have increased their capacity. Good examples and best practice on this can be found in the new booklet on media reform. The Fojo-IMS programme supported process leading up to the adoption of the new liberal media law that was approved in 2021 through support to the Law Working Group and other civil society support. Institutional capacity support to key partners through partner agreements; Ethiopia Media Council (EMC), Mersa Media Institute, Editors Guild of Ethiopia (EGE), Ethiopia National Media Support (ENMS) and CARD. The support included institutional capacity support (staff, office, equipment, training, advice) in order for the organisations becoming stronger and more professional in fulfilling their mandate. The programme has supported the registration and formation of the Editors Guild, Ethiopian Community Radio Broadcaster Association (ECRBA) and the Ethiopia Journalism Educators Network (EJEN). Selected partners and other stakeholders have been trained and recognise increased knowledge, awareness and understanding of the media. Key activities in 2023 includes: Ethiopia Media Authority (EMA) • Signed (IMS) a MoU and a project agreement with EMA in June 2023 to promote smooth implementation. • Supported that 10 media directives were printed/ disseminated to relevant actors/public to create more awareness about the media law. • 5 senior leaders from EMA participated in a weeklong experience sharing and institutional exchange visit to Ghana’s state and selfregulatory organs from November 19 to 25, 2023. Ethiopia Media Council (EMC) All 2023, through partner agreement. • conduct a public awareness-raising campaigns to promote the complaint handling mechanism, • Organised a training on the Complaint Handling Manual that was developed in 2022 and on the Code of Conduct that was also done in 2022 • EMC produced and broadcasted a 36-minute television program and PSA on EBC and EBS TV in November and December 2023 to enhance public engagement and information about the system. • EMC They also did a two-day training on fact-checking, hate speech and conflict sensitive reporting for 43 media professionals and journalists in Nov 2023. Ethiopia Community Radio Association The programme supported ECRBA to hold their general assembly meeting on 4th December 2023 where a new board was elected which was key for the legality and compliance of the association. See also Radio Day Ethiopia under 2.2 below. Centre for Advancement of Rights and Democracy (CARD) With the support from the programme, CARD conducted a Project Cycle Management (PCM) training for eight media association staff from November 7-10 to increase partners capacity in project management, leadership and M&E and compliance.

The programme has supported the establishment of organisations such as Radio Broadcaster Association, Editors Guild and EJEN – they are actively participating in the media reform process. Support has been given to strengthen mandates of key actors and organisations like MERSA and the Media Council – and they are operating more professional, creating more cohesion in the sector and trying to push the reform agenda. Key actors are participating (and have been trained) in the media reform and support is given (MERSA, Editors Guild, Media Council, EMA) A significant unexpected result is that journalism educators are leading the critical debate on media reform itself (mainly due to safety reasons). We are seeing signs of more coordination from practitioners but still often scattered and not coordinated, and to remedy this should be prioritised in a sustainable way. Institution capacity building for key actors involved in the media reform process increased their competencies and engagement in the implementation. The support is contributing (slowly) to a stronger media sector and empowering the selected organisations to fulfil their roles. However, the reform process has been halted and building capacity takes time with many hurdles on its way.
